core_obligations: Reformulate the sequence (proof lines 4790-4802): the curve is a projective line so its Picard group is the integers, and the degree of the restriction of the associated invertible sheaf of the curve is minus one; hence it suffices to show that the pullback on Picard groups is injective with image exactly the invertible sheaves whose restriction to the curve is trivial.

Pullback is an isomorphism onto the trivial-on-the-curve part (proof lines 4804-4814): for an invertible sheaf on the contraction the natural map from it to the pushforward of its pullback is an isomorphism away from the image point of the curve by construction, and at that point it reduces after shrinking to the statement that the structure sheaf of the contraction maps isomorphically to the pushforward of the structure sheaf of the blowup, which is the cited computation of the cohomology of the blowup.

Pushforward inverts the pullback (proof lines 4816-4832): for an invertible sheaf on the blowup whose restriction to the curve is trivial, its pushforward is invertible and the adjunction map from the pullback of the pushforward back to it is an isomorphism; both assertions are clear away from the image point and, by flat base change, reduce to the case where the contraction is the spectrum of a regular local ring, where the restriction to the curve being trivial forces the sheaf itself to be trivial by the description of the Picard group of such a blowup.

Conclude (proof lines 4832-4834): the assignment sending an invertible sheaf to its pushforward is an inverse to the pullback map onto the kernel of the restriction map to the curve, which gives the exactness of the displayed sequence; the splitting is given by twisting by multiples of the curve, whose restrictions have the appropriate degrees.
proof_roadmap: Identify the last map with restriction to the curve and reduce to the statement about the pullback on Picard groups.
Show the pullback is an isomorphism onto the sheaves restricting trivially to the curve, using the cohomology of the blowup.
Show the pushforward inverts the pullback, reducing by flat base change to a regular local base, and read off the splitting.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for the contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind the Picard groups fit into a split short exact sequence whose middle map is the restriction of the degree to the curve and whose splitting twists by multiples of the curve (statement lines 4776-4788). The proof (proof lines 4790-4836) identifies the last map with restriction to the curve, shows that the pullback is an isomorphism onto the sheaves restricting trivially, shows that the pushforward inverts it after reducing by flat base change to a regular local base, and exhibits the splitting. H2: a two-claim argument with a flat base change reduction, written out in full.
